paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Taiwan, made in 1979. Red tea is the fully oxidised tea English calls black tea. On the island it goes back to the Japanese period, when it was first made at Yuchi near Sun Moon Lake, though the island is known above all for [oolong](taiwan:known-for). This label names only [Taiwan](taiwan:on-a-label). That says the leaf grew on the island and nothing more about which area or garden it came from.

Red tea has no [tradition of ageing](red:ageing). It is made to be drunk within a year and a half to three years, while it keeps its first quality. At forty-seven years, this leaf has gone far past the usual life of the style.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
